messages.author: 1de1f9aed0e330b1
messages.subject: Shiny-server set-up problem
parts:
Hi  - I have successfully set up shiny server on a Digital Ocean droplet under ubuntu 16.04, and am using my own domain name.  I installed my own apps and they are working fine.  When I initially installed shiny server, the "Welcome to Shiny Server!" page had the app and Rmarkdown content displaying correctly in the right hand windows.  I have been working on my server since then (unattended upgrades etc, disabling root access via SSH etc. and a few other things) and now the "Welcome to Shiny Server!" page has grey spaces in the windows.  

Although this does not seem to affect my own apps, I am worried that I have messed up some permissions or something.   I think the top window uses the "hello" app under /shiny/sample-apps and this seems to display fine on its own (i.e. from <<mydomainname>>/shiny/sample-apps/hello) whereas I think the lower window uses "rmd" which only displays the words "Shiny Doc" at the top when displayed on its own (i.e. via <<mydomainname>>/shiny/sample-apps/rmd), so maybe that issue is related to the greyed out windows.

The shiny-server.log file contains one error that occurs a few times, but they were from a few days ago, so not sure if they are related to this issue or not.  The error is:

"Failed to render error 500 page: Can't set headers after they are sent"
 
There are also some warnings in the log file:

"Running as root uneccesarily is a security risk...." (e.g. this shows when unattended upgrades are run).

and

"RobustSockJS collision: gkEs1....." 

Can you advise what I might have done wrong here please?  

Many Thanks.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny-server set-up problem
parts:
I believe the latest Shiny Server version may solve #1 and #3--can you try it, and if it doesn't help, email me your shiny-server.log file?

For #2, that's just telling you that with the configuration you have, you can change your startup script to run as your run_as user instead of root.
http://docs.rstudio.com/shiny-server/#running-shiny-server-with-root-privileges

From memory, I think you do this by changing /etc/systemd/system/shiny-server.service; under the [Service] section you can set User=shiny and Group=shiny.
